utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Re, are you ready to continue the examination-in-chief of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I have to apologise. What I'm receiving is the Albanian channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before we go on to further, I just want to ask you to clarify a few things from Friday afternoon, and one of them is that you mentioned that, page 84 of the transcript, on the day that there was fighting at Ramush Haradinaj's house on the 24th of March, 1998, there was a police commander who told you it was unsafe to remain there because Ramush Haradinaj and his group were armed and anything could happen. I just want to ask you: Which police organisation was that police commander from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. There were a lot of police around; therefore, I didn't know that particular one. All I saw was certain ranks displayed on his epaulette.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Another point I wish to clarify was you told the Court on Friday about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, from the answer I take it the witness misunderstood the question. He says: "I didn't know that particular one," whereas I think you were not asking about the identity of the police officer but what organisation the police officer was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it's not clear to Your Honours, I will clarify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, are you saying that you did not know which police organisation the commander was from, or you did not know him personally, or both?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You also testified on Friday about an incident that happened on the road to Gllogjan before the March 24th fighting at the Haradinaj house when some armed men stopped you on the road. I just want you to clarify this: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in camouflage with black Balaclavas, a slit for the eyes and for the mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just describe a little bit more fully what you mean by "camouflage"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage, in all sort of colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mean camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Friday, this is at page 83 of the transcript, you mentioned a Haxhija Haradinaj. Who is Haxhija Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the late uncle of Ramush Haradinaj. He owned a house just next to his, a stone's-throw away, a brand new house, and the other was 20 or 30 years old and that was adjacent to my own land.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You also mentioned a person called Kamil Haradinaj. Who is Kamil Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Qamil Haradinaj. This was his cousin, the son of Haxhija.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Friday when we stopped, on Friday evening, you were telling the Trial Chamber about being brought to what you described as KLA headquarters, and Besnik Haradinaj questioning you in an upstairs room. One of the things you said that he said to you was: "He was taunting me, trying to rile me, trying to abuse me. How many policemen were there in Decani, why was I in the village, why didn't I apply for a permit from them, that sort of thing." When you said "why was I in the village," which is the question I think he was asking you, what village were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said he said to you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village, I was referring to Dubrava, my village, my house. He was asking why didn't I ask for a permit from them to go, and there's another thing. Why didn't we join them, that is what he said, all sorts of questions that he was asking with the explicit purpose of taunting me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you understand him to mean when he said -- when he asked you why you hadn't asked for a permit from them to go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they thought they were the authority in the area. As of the day of the killing, as far as I know, the police were no longer allowed inside the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which killing are you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otovic's killing, Miodrag Otovic, when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know the police were no longer allowed there from that day onwards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I heard people talk about this around Decani, where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That this was a dangerous thing, that it was dangerous to go there, it was difficult to go to Rznici where the station was, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of people were saying that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were saying that sort of thing, the local residents were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Serb or Albanian?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to ask you to clarify some of the things about the interrogation that you underwent at Smajl Haradinaj's house on the 18th of April, 1998, and you were telling the Trial Chamber on Friday about Besnik Haradinaj interrogating you in an upstairs room. Was anyone else present when he was interrogating you, apart from him and you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the outset when they first brought us there, Ramush's brother Daut was there and Zeqir Nimonaj as well. After a brief while, after not that long, they went down the stairs and then he asked me whether I felt like having some coffee, and I said yes. And he sent someone down to get some, and then he and I remained in this small room, 2 by 3 or 3 by 3. It was a small room anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described on Friday drinking coffee. You said: "I started choking and I pleaded with him to open the window. He opened the door and I could no longer hold it back. They chucked me out of the room. I was losing consciousness and choking all the time." It may be -- it was a little bit unclear as to who the "they" is. Who is the "they" who chucked you out of the room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He, he, he, he. And just a minute. It wasn't that I was choking. I had a problem with my breathing, but it wasn't on account of the coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started to suffocate, to all practical intents. I was left with no oxygen whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was that? What had happened to you to cause this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were drinking coffee, and the second or third sip that I took, my breathing was interrupted. I was thinking there for a while that they had poisoned me. I asked him to open the window because there was no air, I couldn't breathe properly. Then I asked him to open the door and he did. He took me outside into the corridor, where I eventually fell down, that narrow corridor just outside the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have any documents with you when you went to Smajl Haradinaj's place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did back at my place. It was in my garden, in my front yard, that they took the documents off me. When they took us outside the house and beat us, they ID'd us, although they knew very well who we were. They took my driver's licence away, the traffic licence belonging to my Mazda car, my military booklet, my health registration booklet, health insurance booklet, as well as both sets of keys, the ones to my car and to the school building since I kept those, too. And I kept them together, both sets, the car keys and the school keys, I kept them on the same ring. The keys to the school building were returned to me by them that afternoon, but they kept all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to be clear, this was before --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The keys to the school building, the keys to the school building were the ones that they eventually returned, that particular set.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To be clear on this, this happened before you went to Smajl Haradinaj's house or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. It was in my front yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before or after you went to Smajl Haradinaj's place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before, before, before, in my front yard. After the front yard, they took me to Smajl Haradinaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were being interrogated in the upstairs room, where was Veselin and Mijat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that narrow corridor. They were being guarded by their own soldiers, sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know they were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the door was opened, I saw them right there, and they were the ones who had brought us all together as a group to that corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the corridor on the top floor or the bottom floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The top floor, just next to the room. Here is the corridor and there is the room, and there's a room in that corridor -- there's a door in that corridor that leads to that small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear them, Veselin and Mijat, when you were in the room being interrogated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you hear whether anything was happening to them at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for as long as I was being interrogated. Later on, that's different, then I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to when you were -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: While we are waiting, can you explain a little more what "later on" -- you said: "That's different, then I did," what you then saw or heard. Do you remember that question? That was dealing with Veselin and Mijat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard them beat them. First, they brought Veselin inside, I heard them beat him, and I heard him moan and cry for help. There is one thing that I forgot to tell you. When I came in, there was a club on the table, a tripartite club, as it were. It had a leather handle, it had some sort of a spring, and then a continuation with some sort of a ball at the end, which is an implement that they obviously used to beat them, first Veselin and then subsequently Mijat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's just go back for a moment to what happened when you lost -- when you lost consciousness.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly when I lost consciousness, but when I came to again Veselin and Mijat were still beside me. I heard them massage me and I woke up. They were trying mouth-to-mouth, and they were trying that sort of thing. I must say that I lost consciousness several times, not just that once, it happened several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you lose consciousness in relation to the incident you just described to Judge Hoepfel, which was your hearing them beating Veselin and Mijat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I came to, after I came to, the first time I came to. When I first lost consciousness, they were the ones who massaged me back to life and gave me mouth-to-mouth respiration, and then I lost consciousness again, and then I came to without anyone's help at all, and it was then that I heard them, because later on there was no one left there to help me, so I came to naturally, you might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which -- which soldiers were there at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside there was Zeqir, he was the loudest; and Daut; and Besnik, as well. I'm not sure if his name was Besnik. I knew that he was Rasim's son, the uncle and brother of the accused Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've just mentioned Ramush, did you see him there at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in that room. Ramush came by later in the course of that day with five or six other soldiers accompanying him. I was lying on the floor in that corridor, since I was unable to move. I wasn't allowed to move either. He came by with five or six of his soldiers, they were his escort, I suppose, I don't know. He came in, he shoved me with his leg, and he said, Hello neighbour, do you recognise me? I said, No, I don't, and then he kicked me in the back saying that I would eventually learn who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How hard did he kick you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it seemed hard enough to me. At the time it felt hard enough since he was wearing those military boots.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage bottoms and some sort of a jumper on top. In his right hand, he was carrying a short automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were the five or six soldiers accompanying him, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I was prone and was hardly able to have a proper look. The more I looked, the worse I felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you injured as a result of his kicking you in the back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. Later when I underwent surgery, I'm not sure what the doctors found.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did the other soldiers there present react when Ramush Haradinaj came in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They greeted him, the ones who were watching me. Sometimes there were more of them, four or five, but sometimes there would only be one or two left, depending.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did they react or relate to him or his presence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came by, they would greet him; that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember if they called him anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the time. They just greeted him with their fists, you know, that sort of greeting. He came in -- because off that corridor there is a door leading to that guest-room that I told you about, the -- the corridor is no more than 2 metres long. It's a very small one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did anyone appear to be in charge of the soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He seemed to be the one in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What gave you the impression that Ramush Haradinaj was in charge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them greet him, and from the outset they were saying that he was the commander. So that went a long way in terms of convincing me that this was, in fact, the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean "from the outset they were saying he was the commander"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time that the story started circulating that he was the commander -- I can't say because I hadn't seem him for quite a long time until, or rather, before that day. Ever since those statements that they had made to the police, that he and the 24 that he was armed and was the commander, and then that evening what I heard when Otovic was attacked and killed, that evening or the next day -- they showed this on TV, the arms, the weapons that were seized, some uniforms, that sort of thing. So that struck me as some sort of confirmation of what they had been saying all along.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A few moments ago, you told the Trial Chamber that he came in, he shoved me with his leg, and he said, Hello, neighbour, do you recognise me? And then you said, No, I don't, and then he kicked you in the back. Did you, in fact, recognise him when he came in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I knew him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you say, No, I don't recognise you, when he asked you if you did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because virtually we were one of the first to be arrested or captured in the area. It was for fear of saying that I knew him, it was for fear of getting killed, otherwise one of us could later have gone on to the police and told them about it or something. One thing I must say, he wasn't the only one to ask me at the time. His brother -- his cousins came over, too, Padram [phoen], Smajl's son, who wore glasses and was wearing civilian clothes, small glasses with square frames. And he came to ask me, Neighbour, do you recognise me? I didn't answer any of them. Naim, Smajl's elder son, had round-rimmed glasses and he asked me the same thing, Neighbour, do you know me? And I said no to each and every one of them. And then the son of Mustafa, he had been abroad quite a long time, he came over that day and asked me the same question. I gave the same answer to everyone, No, I don't know you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said: "It was for fear of saying that I knew him, it was for fear of getting killed." Why did you think if you said you didn't know him that you would be okay?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like that, just the sort of thing you'd expect, you know, when you don't know someone. I was just sort of hoping that they would just let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your psychological state when Ramush Haradinaj shoved you and kicked you in the back? How were you feeling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for moving about, well, I wasn't able to. Mentally, not too bad actually. Since you see that I'm able to remember every tiny detail, that means I wasn't feeling too bad after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about your physical injuries at that point, when he kicked you, what were they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to having blood on my face from the beatings, I didn't actually have any open wounds. As for internal injuries, my pancreas was ruptured, my stomach in two different places, the colon, the stomach walls were crushed. You might say large-scale internal injuries, a whole lot of pain, enormous pain, and this feeling of suffocation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you already sustained those injuries at the point when Ramush Haradinaj kicked you, or did you sustain those injuries later, or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were Veselin and Mijat when Ramush Haradinaj kicked you in the back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that room being beaten, the small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that in the same room you were in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, the small one. It's different. I was lying down on the floor in the corridor all the time, that whole day almost until we were released. And they were being beaten and mistreated in that small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know they were being beaten and mistreated in that small room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because where I was lying, it was just next to that door. It's a simple wooden door. I could hear their screams. I could hear Zeqir and Daut shouting at them, all three of them, and abusing them, and I knew all those three lads, we were together day in and day out, I was familiar with their voices.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened after Ramush Haradinaj kicked you in the back and asked you if you recognised him and you said you didn't, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went into that small guest-room -- you mean, what happened to me? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened in that house that you saw, both to you and your brother and cousin? Just tell the Court what you saw and heard.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said: "Ramush Haradinaj went into the small guest-room," was that the room in which your brother and cousin were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you see what --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That was in a different room, the small room. The guest-room was the larger one, and they were being kept in that small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what happened after -- after your encounter with Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I continued to lie on the floor until a moment later on when another one came by. They called him the Russian, perhaps because he was blond. I didn't know him. He walked down the corridor and kicked me several times very severely. He held a pipe in his hand, a sewer pipe or something like that, and used that to crack me over the shoulders and over the forehead. There was blood on my head. He was abusing me and shouting at me, What we're doing to you is nothing. Do you know what the police are doing to our lads? He beat me black and blue and just left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just describe in more detail what you mean by he beat you black and blue. What did he do to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He kicked me and hit me with that pipe, some sort of a sewer pipe made of metal must have been about a metre long. I was on the floor -- I was on the floor all the time because I was unable to stand up, so he hit me on the stomach and wherever he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said before that you lost consciousness a few times. Did you lose consciousness as a result of the Russian mistreating you like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else, if anything, did you see happen to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please, let me add something. I was just about to vomit or was already vomiting when he came by. That's what I'm saying. I was down on the floor starting to vomit. There was one of those soldiers, they had some sort of a blue bucket there, and he gave it to me to vomit to. In the corridor, next to my head, there were three or four crates full of ammunition. Those were open, and there was one with no ammunition in it. And one of them came over to beat me and took that bucket away from me saying, Don't dirty this bucket. And then what he replaced it with was the one empty crate where there was no ammunition in it for me to vomit into.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I vomited blood. He left. I vomited blood, and that -- quite soon after that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so this happened in a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened after you vomited blood?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, we had French for a moment on the English channel, and from what I heard in French we have now not a complete record in English. Witness, could you please repeat your answer when you started saying: "I vomited blood. He left. I vomited blood, and that ..." Could you please repeat what you then said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I heard in French something like the one who had -- who had hit me, but -- did you say that the one that had hit you, that he left or what did you say at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what happened after you vomited blood. What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, one of those soldiers- I remember this quite clearly- his name was Dervishaj -- just a moment, let me try and remember his first name. I know his last name was Dervishaj, I knew his first name but now I can't recall what his name was. He was there guarding me and he told us -- he told me that we would be released. And then after that Mijat and Vesko were taken out, Veselin, that's what I mean. I kept losing consciousness, so the flow of events was interrupted for me because I would come to and then I would again faint. At one point when I came to, Veselin told me that Mijat had been taken out to fix the car so that we could be released, so that we could take his Lada car.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the front yard in front of the house to wash our faces. There was a water-pump there in front of the house. We had to wash the blood off our faces, ears, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is "we" you, your brother, and Veselin Stijovic, your cousin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Since in the meantime Mijat came back and said that Lada was still out of order, that he hadn't been able to repair it. I think he went there with Nasim Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You washed the blood off your face, ears, and so on. Then what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we went back to the guest-room. They carried me to the guest-room. Ramush's father was there, Hilmija. He brought in a Coka-cola and a Fanta, he offered me some to drink and I was still on the floor -- actually, I was lying on the carpet that was there in the room. So he offered me some Coke or some Fanta, I don't know, but it doesn't really matter, but I was unable to drink so I didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were Veselin and Mijat when this was happening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that house for after you were offered a drink?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not long, maybe 20 minutes, half an hour. I don't know exactly. But it was not such a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, Nasim told us -- we had a fig tree in our yard and the winters in our village were quite cold, and my mother put some chaff around this fig tree, some straw, and then Nasim asked us whether we had hid some weapons in there. We told him that this was not the case, but we had to go to our house together with him and another soldier to remove this straw so that they could see that there was -- there were no weapons hidden there, that this was just what it was, a fig tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long were you at your house for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I neglected to tell you how we actually got to the house. We walked there, first to Xhemajl Mushak [phoen] house and then another man came out of a house with a tractor. I don't know his name, although I do know this person. I was unable to walk and Mijat and Veselin had to carry me most of the way, one at one end and the other at the other end, and then they stopped this guy with the tractor and they put me on to this tractor in order to take me to the house, and they walked behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at your house for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not for a long time. This must have taken maybe 20 minutes for this tree -- for the straw to be removed from the tree so that they could see for themselves what it was. Then they went into the house to cut strips from the curtain to tie our eyes. Kika Mijat had to help them do that, and I was in the yard with Veselin. And while we were standing there at the gate an Ascona car came by. They stopped it. I don't know whether it was Nasim or the other guy who actually did it. I can't remember that. This other guy that I didn't know -- so they stopped this car. There were some soldiers in this Ascona car. They handed him the keys and they continued to Glodjane on foot. And after he bound us- my hands were not tied, only Mijat's and Veselin's- but we all had our -- we were all blindfolded. So they put us in this Ascona car. The two of them sat in the front and the three of us were in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did they take you to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to Gramocina [phoen] and en route they stopped several times. They talked to some people, asking them what the situation was, this kind of conversation generally, Hi, lads, what's the situation? Are there any problems? Did the police come, and so on. And they would say, No. And at one point one of them asked them, Why are you letting them go? And Nasim said, These lads are good. They're good boys. And then we went on to Babaloc. So we took the new road from Dubrava to Babaloc. Near the refugee camp where Serbs from Albania were, the refugees from Albania, the state authorities built houses -- houses for them there. When we approached this area, Nasim told us that we should continue forward and that we should not look back. He said, If you look back, I will shoot you. The two brothers carried me, and when -- then they turned away and walked briskly back. My brother left me with Veselin, and then he ran to get some help from the refugees. One of them came in a car. They put me in this car and took me to the health centre in Decani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you earlier said Kika Mijat had to help them to do that, that was cutting off the strips of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's his nickname used by his family. We called him Kika.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And I wanted to ask what kind of car were you speaking of, an Ascona car --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ascona, it's an old car --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: This Opel Ascona? I know this model. And how did you see that when -- you were blindfolded you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they stopped the Ascona before they blindfolded us. So I saw them stop the car in front of my gate. The soldiers went go on to Glodjane on foot, they then blindfolded us and put us in the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was controlling Babaloc at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Siptars.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mean the Albanian --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanians, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you gave evidence earlier that Ramush Haradinaj had come to Smajl Haradinaj's house. How long was he there for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he went into the guest-room, and I didn't see him leave to pass me by, but there was another exit from the guest-room leading to the road itself. There was a staircase that opened directly on to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know how long he was there for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just said a moment ago you went to the health centre in Decani. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber where you went and what treatment you got for your injuries, starting with the health centre in Decani, but pausing.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in Decani we were received by a doctor. I was given a shot - I don't know what kind of a shot it was - and he immediately said that I should be taken to Pec. I was taken there by a civilian vehicle. This was a small health centre. They put me in a small civilian car, and they took me to the Pec hospital, where they X-rayed me. And I was transferred, it was an emergency, to the hospital in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it the same day that you were transferred to the hospital in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day. It all happened in a span of maybe two, three, four hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get to the hospital in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken there in an ambulance from Pec. This was an ambulance of the Pec hospital that was used to transport me to the hospital in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what treatment did you receive at the hospital in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I underwent surgery. I was hospitalised for 28 days. I really started missing my family, and I asked the doctor, the surgeon who operated on me, to ask -- to let me see my family. It was a Friday, and he actually released me on a Friday. I went to Decani to the huts where we lived at the time. I was supposed to return to the hospital on Monday, and on Monday when my family asked me - I couldn't move, you have to know that - when they asked whether the Pristina route was safe and the police told them that the route from Pristina to Pec was actually blocked and that we couldn't move.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stojanovic, while we're coming to that, I just want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please display Exhibit 65 ter 863, can you please display it in Serbian for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be exhibit number P33, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a discharge sheet with case history from Pristina hospital dated the 6th of October, 2005, referring to your being in hospital from the 18th of April --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I never did get my discharge papers, so I don't actually have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, but if you just wait for a moment, you'll see them on the screen in front of you, referring to your stay from the 18th of April, 1998, to the 15th of May, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just make that larger for us, if possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Does that describe the injuries you received and the operation you underwent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but I can't read everything. You would have to scroll down. I don't know whether this is actually the end of the document or not. And, in fact, I'm not an expert in medicine, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It is referring to you, isn't it? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you went to the hospital, who -- did the doctors take a -- what's called a history from you; that is, did they ask you what had happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It says here that the: "Patient was attacked on his own door-step in Metohija by terrorists. They hit him with a rifle-butt and kicked him. He spent 12 hours in their prison, and he was taken to a hospital in Pec." What I want to ask you is this: Do you remember whether it was you who told the staff at the hospital or whether someone else did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it -- how long did you actually spend in the custody of these people from the time in the morning between 8.00 and 9.00 until the time you were released and blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from 8.00 or 9.00 until 4.00 or 5.00, I think that was the time when it actually ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, in the medical report, it said that: "There was a difficult post-operative recovery. The wound healed but became extensively infected. The suture of the duodenum remained in place, so the patient quickly recovered despite the infection in the wound." Did you sustain any lasting injuries as a result of what happened to you on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what can I tell you? All the doctors that I -- that I've seen always asked me for this document for Pristina, although I have not been able to get it. I've tried obtaining this document through various humanitarian organisations when we moved, but I couldn't get this document, and the examinations never revealed anything. I never had this piece of paper that I could show to a doctor because I can't explain to a doctor what the situation -- what happened to me, what kind of injuries I sustained. But I do have consequences, and if I were to show you what my abdomen looks like, I think you would be -- you would see for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I want you to tell the Trial Chamber is what medical treatment you've received since then and whether you still -- whether you suffered any lasting injury; and if so, for how long? So, firstly, tell the Trial Chamber about any medical treatment after you were released from hospital.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For six months I had to go to the health centre in Decani to have my wounds dressed, because the wound was weeping all the time and I had to go there three times a day to have my wound re-bandaged there in the health centre in Decani. The situation there was very bad; there were just two or three nurses and a doctor who was not a specialist in this area. But because there was this war going on, I had to go there; I had no other choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And after those six months, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wound healed, it was no longer weeping, so that was basically it. I still have some consequences. I break out in a sweat a lot; I dream about those events at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you off work after sustaining these injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long were you off work for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I still don't work, because Dr. Andrija Tomanovic told me at that time that I should not lift anything heavier than 5 kilos, that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to lift anything more than 5 kilos now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I could do it, but I shouldn't. I must not because after all I'm not an expert and he is, and that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are the injuries you received on the 18th of April, 1998, the reason why you haven't worked since then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to have a look at a video, which is Exhibit 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The video will be displayed in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the -- is there any -- what's the spoken text on the video, what language?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's in English, it's digitised. It's in Serbian and in English, it's digitised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The transcript is 65 ter 37 and 38, which is in Albanian, English, and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll just read the English from the screen. Is that what I understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will not be read aloud, because otherwise we'll need to have it translated into French. But we treat it as an exhibit rather than as part of the transcript. So, therefore, we just look at it without any English being spoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Madam Registrar, it would be number...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P34, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Re, I take it that P33, having heard what the witness said, there might be a copy -- a spare copy somewhere for the witness to take home in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the video can be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Stojanovic, was that you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember the cameras coming in? Were you conscious at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to any journalists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, yes, and then I refused to talk to any of them because I just couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What state were you in when the cameras and the journalists came into the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you just been operated on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the intensive care unit depicted here, this is where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your evidence today and on Friday, you said you were taken to what you thought was -- what you described as the KLA headquarters. Why did you think that Smajl Haradinaj's house was the KLA headquarters?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that's what I had heard from them. Even that day, I told you they were saying, What shall we do with these people? And the other guy told them, Take them to HQ. I didn't know there was one or, indeed, where it was before I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The house and the property which you described on Friday which is next to the Ramush Haradinaj family compound or property, who owns that house? I mean your house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which house? On my land? That one is owned by Ljubica Stojanovic, my mother. This is land, an estate, belonging to our family which we inherited from our father.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long has it been in your family for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My grandfather, then my father and then I. We have all the documents to show that the property belongs to us, the original purchase documents. When we fled the area, I gave this to the local administration and I received a confirmation in return from them, saying that this was our land, our property, and that no one would be allowed to take it away from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you flee the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't safe. If I had stayed, I would have been killed; that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who do you think would have killed you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like most other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who do you think would have killed you if you had stayed there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those same people who had arrested me, beaten me, and mistreated me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you referring to KLA members and Ramush Haradinaj and his associates?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. There were people who were arrested after me; for example, Mirko Vlahovic; Miro Vlahovic; Dana, a lady; and her daughter whose name I think is Dara; and her daughter, too, whose name I can't remember; the Radunovics, husband and wife. It was a week after I had been arrested, they too were arrested, never to turn up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was it that you fled the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of April, 1999, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was -- I withdraw that. You said on Friday, the last time you lived in your house was the 24th of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Friday? My house? Are you asking about my home? The previous question. Are you asking about my home or the Decani area?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm talking about your home next to the Haradinaj family compound.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of March, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I may have missed the point in the last question. The witness testified that he left the area the 12th of April, 1999. Then you say you said on Friday the last time you lived in your house was the 24th of March, 1998, and then the witness confirmed that. What was -- I didn't understand, it's just to put the two dates one next to another so that we know that he left his house in 1998, 24th of March, and then the area later?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To finish, I want to show you two more photographs, Mr. Stojanovic. Firstly, there's an overhead photograph of -- which is Exhibit Number 1210.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If that could be displayed in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P35, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking at this one, Mr. Stojanovic, it does actually have Gllogjan and surroundings written on the top, can you recognise that is an aerial photograph of Gllogjan and the village of Rznic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer again, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the air, yes, I do recognise it. It's an aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see where your property is on that -- on that map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see where the Haradinaj family compound is on that map?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe if we could blow up the bit underneath where it says "Gllogjan." Can you zoom in a bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We've made it larger, does that assist you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I see it, but I can't be specific enough. You can't really tell the houses in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1106.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P36, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a house with a cow in front of it. Can you identify that house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a house in Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell us whose house it is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this might be Zeqir Xheladin's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is it in relation to your house, your property?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at the village, in front of Smajl's house, in front of Smajl's house. It's not too near my own property unless something has been changed over. It did look a lot like this when I was still down in the area --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand the last bit of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may assist if the witness just simply for a second were to remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, could you please take off your headphones for a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's no dispute that this is the Haradinaj family compound depicted in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long is it since you've been back to where your property is in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nine years. My own property is in Dubrava, not in Glodjane. They do share a border, though, the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to clarify -- to finish, I just want to clarify one thing and that's -- you said you fled the area, and I want to try and clarify the reason why you left your property, your house, in the village of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, my property, my estate is part of Dubrava officially. It's the last estate in Dubrava, the most out-lying estate if you like, and after my estate, that's where the Glodjane land begins. Why did I flee? For safety reasons, you might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you said before you went for fear of your life, were you referring to leaving your property or were you referring to leaving the Decani area? I just want to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I was referring to was we were leaving provisionally, that's what I thought at the time, I thought that things would soon be back to normal and that we could proceed as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, I'd like to -- witness, part of your answer was lost earlier. Could you please have again a look at this photograph and see whether you can be -- whether you recognise whose house this is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This house could have been added to, in the meantime. It changed over. There could have been an extension. It looks like Hilmi's house, but it wasn't like this when I was there. If it's the same house, extensions have been made to it. This whole part just next to this tree over here wasn't there when I was last physically present in the area. His house was old. One floor, but it wasn't a finished house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a wall around the Haradinaj family compound when you left on the 24th of March, 1998, that's Ramush Haradinaj's compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not around the family compound, but around the yard. There was what we refer to as a fence, a wooden fence, and inside the fence a new wall had been built.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When had the new wall been built?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 24th of March, must have been one of those days just before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know why it was built?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Re. Mr. Emmerson, first of all, it's time for a break I would say. Of course I understood that there's no -- seems to be no disagreement about what this house is, nevertheless I put some questions in relation to the house for other purposes, not to identify the house as such. And I'd like to be informed if major changes were made since 1998 to that house for the same purposes. Then, Mr. Re, yesterday there was a glimpse of hope when you said that you would finish the witness in the scheduled one and a half hour. It was two and a half, as a matter of fact. We'll first have a break, Mr. Stojanovic, and then you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence. I already asked the usher to escort you out of the courtroom because one or two little tiny things. If you, Mr. Usher, would escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'll resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'd like to hear about the approximate time of cross-examination. I did understand that it would take quite some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I expect to be longer with this witness than with the next witness who covers a much the same territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So to the extent that I'm somewhat longer with this witness the time will be significantly made up with a much shorter, I expect, cross-examination of the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think you'll need?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll certainly be completed considerably within two hours, I would hope nearer to an hour and a half but two hours is an outer limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have another question. There was a partly confidential motion filed, I think, it was on Friday, it had to do with videolink. Does the Defence know when it will respond to it, whether it would be an oral response or --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I answer that question immediately after the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- get being information immediately after the break. If the Chamber, of course, would accept an oral answer if there is agreement, if not, the matter is relatively urgent because preparing for a videolink takes approximately one week and if you look at the scheduling we would like to receive an answer as soon as possible. We'll have a break and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour want to deal with those two matters now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if that can be done quickly, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, so far as the videolink application is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- our view is that whilst we would never wish to stand in the way of an application based on medical grounds --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the only short-coming in the document, as we see it, is that there's no attempt to explain why it is that the wife can't be cared for by medical professionals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if that matter can be explored, then perhaps we could revisit it once the answer is to hand, perhaps even tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that that's the only issue to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as -- so far as the Haradinaj Defence team is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at Mr. Guy-Smith and I'm looking at -- who --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- nods yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That was the issue that we collectively discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same, too. Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, the other matter again, perhaps best dealt with with the witness in the absence of the headphones, is the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your headphones for a second? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour has the photograph either in mind or on the screen, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The position is that there was a tree shown in the photograph. Everything to the right of the tree is a building that stands in exactly the position of the building that was on the site at the time. Now, the original building was destroyed by Serbian shelling and fire during 1998, or very largely destroyed, and has been rebuilt. Everything to the left of the tree is an addition that has gone on since then. So to that extent, the witness's recollection - perhaps that's what threw him - is correct; that that portion of the building on the left was added at or after the time that the building was rebuilt following bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's just for the Chamber to be able to make a better assessment of reliability issues. Okay. That's clear. Then -- that's -- then I think we could start cross-examination. Could you put your earphones -- yes. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, you'll now be examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before I start to ask you questions, I want to explain to you in advance the line of questions that I'm going to put to you so that you understand what it is I am asking you about. If you don't understand any question or you want me to explain why I'm asking you it, do please just say so. I'm not going to ask you any questions about your injuries, and may I make it clear at the outset that I am not challenging the fact that you were badly beaten on the 18th of April, 1998, by Albanian villagers from Gllogjan. The questions that I am going to ask you are aimed at exploring the background to this incident and how and why it may have happened, and I'm also going to suggest to you that you are mistaken in your identification of Ramush Haradinaj as a person who was present at Smajl Haradinaj's house while you were detained there. So that is, broadly speaking, the topics or the areas on which I am going to ask you some questions. First of all, I want to deal with that second topic; in other words, what happened to you inside Smajl Haradinaj's building in Gllogjan and the incident where you describe a man you believed to be Ramush Haradinaj walking up the stairs and kicking you in the back and saying to you, Do you recognise me, neighbour? It's that incident I'm going to ask you some questions about; all right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that you went to school with Ramush Haradinaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same school, not the same class. We weren't classmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj, I suggest to you, left Kosovo in 1991 and did not return to live in Kosovo until the end of February 1998. Can I ask you, please, do you say that you saw him at all between 1991 and the occasion on the 18th of April, when you say you saw him inside Smajl Haradinaj's house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't seen him for about ten years, but I did again at Smajl Haradinaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was the first time you'd seen Ramush Haradinaj, if you were right, for ten years?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, the man you've identified as Ramush Haradinaj, you didn't see him at any earlier point on the 18th of April before you say he came up the stairs inside the house, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't before then that I saw him. You understood me well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So you, for example, never saw him outside your house when you and your cousin and your brother were taken from there or at any time on the route down to the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think -- am I right in saying - and I'm taking this from a statement you have made to the Prosecution - that after that incident on the 18th of April, you never saw him again. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So now we can just focus in on that moment when this man walked up the stairs. I want to make sure that I've understood your account of that part of the incident correctly. Now, you've told us, I think, that by the time this man came up the stairs, you had already been badly hurt. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you told us all of the injuries you had sustained had already been sustained before that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to be specific. I had been beaten. I had started to suffocate before that point in time; that is, when he eventually came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you had already lost consciousness on a number of occasions, I think. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, again, so that I've got the sequence correct, from the evidence that you've given so far, you've described three spaces that make up the first floor or the top floor of the house. You've described the corridor, a small room, and a larger guest-room. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that the Judges understand, a guest-room is what's known in Albanian as an "oda." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's called "burjum."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In Serbian perhaps. But it's a large room --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not here to communicate --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj is nodding yes on the answer of witness, although it's not usually my task to -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's a large room typically, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us about an occasion when you were being asked questions by, I think, Besnik, you said, Haradinaj inside that building; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is I thought his name was Besnik. One thing I do know for sure is that he was at Rasim Haradinaj's house. Rasim Haradinaj is the accused person's uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You say it was at Rasim Haradinaj's house. Did you not tell us earlier it was at Smajl Haradinaj's house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Rasim's house. The son of Rasim Haradinaj was interrogating me in Smajl Haradinaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what I had understood. And that interrogation is the one where you asked him to open the window, he gave you a cup of coffee, you choked on it, and then he opened the door. That's the interrogation we're speaking about, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd finished about half my coffee, and then all the rest that followed the interrogation, in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I just want to clarify. Which of those three rooms did that interrogation take place: The large guest-room, the small room, or the corridor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you've told us that when the door was opened and you went out into the corridor, Mijat, your brother, and your cousin Veselin were in the corridor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all brought to the corridor together, all together, all the way from my house to that corridor. And then I was thrown into that small room to be interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So I understand it's a bit -- I'm asking you detailed questions. The question I'm asking you is: When you came out of the small room after being interrogated, when the door was opened, Mijat and Veselin were in the corridor, according to you. Is that right, they were still there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mijat and Veselin and the soldiers guarding them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, but they were -- just so we're clear. Mijat and Veselin were in the corridor when you came out of that room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you told us I think that you lost consciousness again in the corridor on a number of occasions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us of an occasion when you heard Mijat and Veselin shouting whilst they were being ill-treated in another room; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever I came to I would hear that. It wasn't just for a brief while. The beating went on for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Two things, if I may. Which room of the three were they? You were in the corridor, when you heard their shouts were they coming from the large guest-room or from the little room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from the little room, because I was next to the door to the small room, and this was a very narrow corridor and I can be quite certain that they came from the little room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's what I needed to be clear. So the other two were, you say, being ill-treated in the little room, not in the guest-room. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the little room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you be clear, were they in there together or were they taken in separately, one after the other, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They first took Veselin in, as far as I can remember, and then they took Mijat in as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when they took Mijat in, did Veselin come out or did he stay inside; in other words, were two of them in the room at the same time or were they in the room separately, one after the other?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there at the same time, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there was a period of time when you were on your own in the corridor, in the sense that neither of the other two or with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you told us this afternoon that it was while you were on your own in the corridor that the man you say is Ramush Haradinaj came and kicked you in the back. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First he shoved me with his foot in order for me to face him, and then he asked me, Neighbour, do you know me? And when I said, No, he kicked me in the back. This is what I state, and then he told me, Well, you will come to know me well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. My question, Mr. Stojanovic, is simply this: When that incident occurred, that was - you told us earlier on - whilst both of the other two were in the small room and you were in the corridor without either of them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the corridor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, just to be absolutely clear because that doesn't entirely answer my question. When this incident happened with the man you say was Ramush Haradinaj, were -- was either Mijat or Veselin in the corridor with you at that time, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not there. I was the only one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think you've already told us this afternoon that nobody mentioned the word "commander" or addressed Mr. Haradinaj as you thought it was with the name "commander" in your presence that afternoon, did they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my presence. They simply stood up and greeted him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Could you repeat how they greeted him? You described that already in your former examination, but you made a sign with a hand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A fist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: The fist to the head. Thank you. That was a sign --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the record perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the record perhaps reflect the witness raised his right fist with his elbow out and put it to his forehead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that at least three other people said the same thing to you, Do you recognise me, neighbour, that afternoon; is that correct? At least three others?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it more than three other people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three people that I can remember: Agron; Nasim; and Mustafa Zeq, Islam's son. Agron Naim, not Nasim, but Naim, Smajl's son, his eldest son.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the room that the man you say was Ramush, the room that he walked into you've told us was the guest-room; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So he did not walk into the small room where the other two men were being detained?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, you didn't see him walk into the room at any time, the small room, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him walk into the small room.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us that after he walked into the big room, you didn't see him again, is that right, that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you had to try and estimate it for the Judges, how long do you think it would have taken this man to get from the top of the stairs to have the conflict with you, where you say he kicked you and so on, and then to walk into the guest-room? Roughly how many, if you can put it in seconds for us, how long did that go on for, do you think?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a matter of seconds. It was at least five or six minutes because he stopped next to me. He didn't just pass; he stopped there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the conversation that you've described, was that the only conversation that took place during this five minutes, where he said to you, Do you recognise me, neighbour?
