utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But he also spoke to his soldiers. They greeted him, he greeted them back, and they had a discussion, but this was the only thing that he told me. This was the only conversation that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you pick up at all what the discussion he was having with the soldiers was about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to understand that I didn't really care about what they were talking about because I was thinking about my own problems, how I could actually get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I quite understand that. Mr. Stojanovic, do you think, given how badly injured you had been and given the fact that you were drifting in and out of consciousness, you might become confused about the sequence of these events or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask, please, that you be shown a witness statement that you made on the 2nd of November, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is in English and in Albanian, but we don't need that, the Defence 1D020426 and there is a B/C/S version at 65 ter 1211 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to show that to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar that will be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be D22, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can just go, please, to the -- on the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, this is a translation into Serbian of the statement that you have signed on the 2nd of November, 2001 -- I'm sorry, it's the Albanian that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The B/C/S version should be 65 ter 1211. It's separate. I see. I understand the Prosecution have hard copies of the B/C/S version. I wonder if the witness might be given a hard copy of the statement that he made in Serbian -- or the Serbian translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And could we please have the English version 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you're going to tender which version, which language version?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I will tender the English and Albanian versions, and we will link-up the B/C/S version in due course so that there will be a single exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they'll -- yes, they'll all three, English, Serbian, and Albanian, will be under the same number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I think you saw that witness statement before you gave evidence on Friday, didn't you? Mr. Stojanovic, is there a problem with translation? Ah --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this statement, but I saw quite a few errors in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Errors, defects, that make it different from what I actually said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can look at the translations separately, Mr. Stojanovic. I just want to look at what you are recorded as having said. First of all, you read this statement through before you gave evidence -- just let me finish. You read this statement through before you gave evidence on Friday, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can you please -- if you just look through from the beginning of the statement, the paragraph numbers -- the paragraphs may not be the same and they're not numbered. If you could find the seventh full paragraph, if you just count the full paragraphs through to the seventh full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could have the English on the screen, please, at 0426, that's the statement itself, and we would want 0 -- the number we have here is 24692, so it's the third page of the statement in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The statement should be document identification 0426 in English. Do we have that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just, Mr. Stojanovic, just be --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Don't worry about the screen. If you concentrate on the Serbian version, which you've got in hard copy, if you could read over to yourself, please, the seventh paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me, what page is this seventh paragraph on?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The difficulty is that the pages will not necessarily correspond. If you could just count through from the beginning of the text of the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if you read the very beginning of that paragraph in English, then it will be translated for the witness so that he can find his way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a paragraph which begins, Mr. Stojanovic: "They were all wearing green guerilla-type uniforms ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's a short paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does Your Honour have it in English on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It must be a short paragraph after the long paragraph which deals with several names, and the last sentence of the long paragraph is: "The other three were my neighbours I have known."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. We have a problem because we have an Albanian version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, can you find a paragraph which starts: "They were all wearing green guerilla-type uniforms and they all wore black berets"? Can you find a paragraph starting with that line?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It will be roughly on the second or third page. Perhaps if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we put it on the ELMO, and then we're able to see what the witness also sees, and we could try to assist him. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be that I might be able to count through and show him which paragraph I'm referring to, rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I try that first?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you just pass the statement to me for a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do you have more than one copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's page 4, just about halfway down the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've placed a cross, Mr. Stojanovic, at the passage I want you to look at, please. And if you could just read those paragraphs. Perhaps we can give you an opportunity to have a look at them yourself for a moment, down to the part where you discuss Ramush Haradinaj and including that part. Have you had an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. In the paragraph which begins: "They were all wearing green guerilla-type uniforms ...", you describe the questioning that this man Besnik Haradinaj conducted inside the room. Do you agree? That's what you're describing in that paragraph; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's then a paragraph that begins: "I was badly injured while in our house before, and I started to lose consciousness and pass out. I started to choke, and they pulled me from the room. They did not strike me at all during this time because I was already injured so badly. I had blood all over my face and head. I was losing consciousness again. I was lying in the hallway on the concrete for a while, sometimes regaining consciousness and could hear Mijat and Veselin's screams coming from inside the room I had been inside. I did not see them take them inside this room." First of all, is that correct, that passage? Just the passage I've read to you, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were put inside this room, yes, I was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, did you -- I don't know if we got the whole of your answer. When you got -- when you were put inside the room --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you ask me a specific question so that I could see what is it that you want me to tell you, what you're asking me for?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course I can. I was originally just asking you, Mr. Stojanovic, whether the passage that I've just put to you is correct? Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that it follows that you were in and out of consciousness whilst on the corridor and didn't see Mijat and Veselin being taken into the small room. Is that right? You were unconscious when Mijat and Veselin were taken into the small room. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veselin, yes, but Mijat was put into this room later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see him being put into the room, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mijat? You mean Mijat?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Because you can see that in the statement you've been recorded as saying: "I did not see them take them inside the room." "Take them inside the room." Do you see --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the first one, but yes as to the second one, the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay. If we just look at the lines which follow, you give a list of names and descriptions of people, and at the bottom of that paragraph you refer to someone called Isuf Verizaj, and you say that man told you --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Not Isuf Verizaj but Jusuf Dervishaj. This goes to show that there are quite a lot of defects in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. The gentleman that is there referred to, you say Jusuf Dervishaj, the statement records him saying to you: "Don't be afraid we will let you go." And you say: "This man was my neighbour and I saw him and recognised his voice, too. I passed out then again." Is that right? After that man spoke to you, you passed out then again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fainted a number of times, so I think that this is probably correct, but since nine years have passed, I am -- I'm afraid unable to remember every little detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely understand that, Mr. Stojanovic, and that's what I put to you a moment ago, that having regard to the condition you were in, remembering the precise sequence of what took place may be difficult for you and it may have become confused in your mind. Now, I want, if I may, to just look at the next paragraph because after you describe Mijat and Veselin being inside the room and having heard their screams, you then say: "After a while I awoke again. I saw Ramush Haradinaj coming up the stairs with some soldiers. Ramush walked up to me and kicked me in my back. Ramush asked me then, Do you recognise me, neighbour? When I answered, No, he said if you don't know me, you will know me. I saw Veselin and Mijat on the floor in the corridor. They were next to me. They were" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment. I'm lost a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I apologise. Does Your Honour have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Did you continue with the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a paragraph beginning: "After a while ..." Does Your Honour have that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's the following paragraph on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Same page? In English?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's in English, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in English, it's still the same paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. "After a while" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, does Your Honour have that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Does this mean after the sentence: "I passed out then again ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly, this is after the description of Veselin and Mijat being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we can go to that paragraph again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So it is after the long paragraph that we discussed before so make sure that the witness knows exactly what paragraph we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness finds it in his own language page 5, I think the new paragraph starting approximately the seventh line from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I noticed the witness turning over the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just go through that paragraph again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "After I while I awoke again I saw Ramush Haradinaj coming up the stairs with some soldiers?" You then describe the incident that you've told us about and you then say he said, If you don't know me, you will know me" --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "I saw Veselin and Mijat on the floor in the corridor. They were next to me. They were conscious. I passed out again and awoke, and Veselin was there but Mijat was gone?" Now, the account that's recorded in this statement, Mr. Stojanovic, is that at the time the man you say was Ramush Haradinaj came up the stairs, Veselin and Mijat were conscious in the corridor beside you and they had already been taken into the room where they had been beaten. Now, that's what the statement records. Can you help us with that at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can. In the statement it appears that all of this happened within a span of one minute, if you're reading the statement, but you have to insert some pauses here because first the thing with Ramush happened. Then after a while, after some time, perhaps I fainted again, I came to and I saw Mijat and Veselin next to me. So please, do not attempt to challenge what I'm saying here because I know very well what happened and what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Leaving the times aside, Mr. Stojanovic, just looking at the sequence, in this statement you were recorded as having said that Mijat and Veselin had been taken into the small room and beaten before this man you describe as Haradinaj came up the stairs, and that by the time he came up the stairs they had been removed from the small room and were back in the corridor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- would you please -- could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness, I think, gave an explanation which at least -- when the statement reads: "I saw Veselin and Mijat on the floor in the corridor ...", was that when you saw Mr. Haradinaj coming up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. First he kicked me, and then after a while, at a later stage, I fainted again. And then when I came to, I saw them in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've told us this afternoon that at the time this incident occurred you couldn't recognise the other soldiers because you were prone, that is face down, and hardly able to have a proper look. That was your evidence this afternoon. Is that a fair description of the position you were in when the man you say was Mr. Haradinaj came up the stairs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that I was face down; I said just that I was lying down on my left or on my right side if I managed to turn over, because it was very difficult for me to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then that's my mistake because the word I've written down in your testimony is "prone," which to me means face down. Perhaps that's now how it was intended to be translated, but you did tell us, didn't you, that you were hardly able to have a proper look and the more you looked the worse it felt?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I felt worse, but this was such a small room. It was less than 2 by 2 metres. It's such a small room. I already explained that in a corner of that room there were some ammunition crates. I was there on the floor, and the troops. It was impossible for somebody to pass by without me noticing him or her, provided of course I was conscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, obviously. That's one of the things I need to ask you about, because you are drifting in and out of consciousness during this process. You're lying on the floor, and you've told us that you were - to use your words - hardly able to have a proper look at the other soldiers that were there. So what I'm trying to explore with you is: How much of the time whilst you were lying there do you think you were conscious and how much of it were you unconscious?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. When one is unconscious, it's very difficult for one to tell for how long that might be. That is why there are a great many details that I'm not familiar with and that the other two witnesses might know who were there, details that I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I read to you, Mr. Stojanovic, without, I think, going through the time-consuming process of putting it up on the screen, can I read to you a passage from a statement that you made on the 26th of May, 2002, to the Prosecution, and I'll read it slowly so it can be translated to you. It's not the document you have in front of you, it's the second statement that you made. You said: "I remember that after I had been beaten at the HQ, Ramush came to ask me whether I knew him and then saying that soon I would, he kicked me once in the back and then went to the room where my brother and cousin had been taken a while before."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the brother, not the cousin, the guest-room. This may be a mistranslation, but I'm telling you what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can check the translation, Mr. Stojanovic, but the record of what you said is that the man walked into the room where your brother and cousin had been taken a while before. That wouldn't be right, though, would it, on your present evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the small room, the guest-room, the large one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're also recorded as saying: "He did not introduce himself to me as a commander, but I heard the KLA soldiers addressing him as such." Again, that would be wrong as well, presumably, because you didn't hear the KLA soldiers addressing him as "commander," did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in so many words, but they did greet him, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And after this incident, you told us that you saw Hilmi Haradinaj at one point. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Hilmi towards the end in that room when he gave us some Coca-Cola and Fanta.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there a time when you were outside in the yard by Smajl Haradinaj's house together with Veselin and Mijat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the yard by Smajl Haradinaj's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you were never -- there was never a period of time when you and your brother Mijat and Veselin were standing outside in the yard by Smajl Haradinaj's house and being held there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smajl Haradinaj, yes. I thought you were asking about Hilmi's yard because you had been asking me questions about Hilmi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, don't worry. We'll put -- we'll put the question clearly. Was there a period of time then when you and your brother and your cousin were standing guarded outside Smajl Haradinaj's property, in the yard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they took us outside the house to wash up, there were guards behind us. We were using that water-pump, and we were trying to wash our faces. Hilmi was just beneath the staircase. He was seated there, and then he went back to the room with us. That didn't appear to me to matter very much, but he was with us up there when he gave us the fruit juice, when he gave us some pie.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You never saw Ramush Haradinaj at any point in the yard outside Smajl Haradinaj's house, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to move on now to some other topics. You told us, Mr. Stojanovic - and I'm just exploring some background questions for a moment - you told us that on the 18th of April, you recognised one of the people who came up to the house, you recognised a Chinese machine-gun. And Mr. Re asked you how you knew this, and you said: "I had been to reserve officer's school and I took a number of classes on weapons, so I knew" --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back in the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So I wanted to be clear: How long before this incident on the 18th of April had you had your training in reserve officer's school in the military?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was back in 1986 and 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So about 11 years or thereabouts earlier?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I ask you one or two questions, please, about your brothers? Apart from yourself, have I got it right, there were four other brothers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There was Mijat, and you've told him his -- his nickname was Kika. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was, I think, several years older than you, is that right, is several years older than you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, two.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two years, thank you. Then there's Predrag?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our eldest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so how much older than you is Predrag?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure when exactly he was born, but he was the eldest brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then there's Vladimir or Vlado. Is his nickname Vlado?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is he older than you or younger than you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Older.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so can you just explain to us where he comes. Is he younger than Predrag and older than Mijat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then who is the fourth brother, what's his proper name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veselin.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's Veselin Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is his nickname Vesko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how old in relation to you is Veselin Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's older. I am the youngest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, no misunderstanding, Veselin Stojanovic is obviously not the same person as Veselin Stijovic who you referred to at one point on Friday as your cousin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, not the same person. Stijovic is a relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. You have an immediate brother called Veselin; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Predrag, your oldest brother, was a police officer, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When did he join the police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the year he joined, but he still worked together with the Siptars in the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But he'd been a police officer for some years before 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you see him in uniform from time to time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever come to know what sort of weapon or weapons he had as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we've seen --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, just a minute, please. I didn't, the reason being he lived in Djakovica. He would sometimes come over to give us a hand with the farm, but normally he resided and worked in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovic, we've seen some official records that show that by March 1999, he was a member of the paramilitary police. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramilitary police, no, that is not true. It's not that I don't know about it. It is most certainly not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, you've heard of the PJP, have you? PJP, do those initials mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The PJP, the paramilitary police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please try to expand for me to know what that means, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can give you the full name in Serbian, if that would assist you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, that's what I'd like, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if you just bear with me, I'll spell it for the interpreter. It's Posebne, P-o-s-e-b-n-e; Jedinice, J-e-d-i-n-i-c-e; Policije, P-o-l-i-c-i-j-e.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never even heard of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when you tell us categorically that your brother was not a member of the paramilitary police you're not able to tell us one way or the other whether he was a member of that organisation, are you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you is he was a watchman. He was a police officer who most of the time was spending his time as a watchman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll come back to what he was doing in a little while, if I may. What about Veselin, as far as you know, did he ever join the police at all or the police reserve at any time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither the reserve nor any kind at all, not the police, not the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know anybody else called Veselin Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Dubrava, not where we lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so do I take it that neither you nor either of your other two brothers, Mijat or Vladimir, were members of the police reserve. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're free to conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us then, please, between January and March 1998 who was living at your house? Who was living there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between January and March, I was, my mother was, my sister was. I worked in Decani at the school that I mentioned. My sister would go to Djakovica, she worked there, she worked in a shop, and my mother was retired. Mijat would sometimes come. He had lived in Belgrade for a long time. The last couple of years he was there, he was selling some sort of dye, some sort of oxidised dye, industrial. So he would go to that shop but he would often come over, back to his old home and spend the night with us. He was, however, a resident of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you whether either you or any other member of your family kept weapons at your home between January and the 24th of March, 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What weapons did you keep at your home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother had a pistol and a hunting rifle that my father had left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you use to carry the pistol around with you, yourself, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother's? You mean my mother's pistol? I didn't have a pistol. The pistol belonged to my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you carry it around with you when you were away from the home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you about the incident when you were stopped by four masked men in Gllogjan. You've told us that they asked you some questions --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us that they asked you some questions and searched you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They searched me and they searched the car as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did they tell you what they were looking for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't explain what they were after, but they searched both me and the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did they find a gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your car?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my car either.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did you have to sign a piece of paper to say that they had given you back your gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who said they give me back anything? They hadn't found anything to begin with. Did I sign a statement? Yes, I did, that they had not mistreated me, to that effect. That's what they asked me to do. They dictated a statement to me, and I wrote it down that they hadn't mistreated me, that they hadn't beaten me, which after all was true, at least it was true for that particular evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've asked me a question, and it's one of those rare occasions where I'm permitted to answer it. And it's your mother who says that they found a gun on you; she's made a statement to that effect, that they found a pistol on you and that you were required to sign --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother, my mother is an old woman. I signed the statement. I was the one who had been searched. How can my mother or anyone else on earth, for that matter, know anything about that except for myself? It wasn't just once that they actually physically frisked me during that time that they stopped me; they frisked me about five times.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You presumably discussed this incident with your mother, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the police about that incident. I'd reported to the police, as any citizen indeed should.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please see Rule 65 ter number 1161?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be -- oh, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D23, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm going to have to read this passage to you because we don't have it in Serbian, but we have heard evidence from the person who compiled this report after conducting an interview with your mother, in which she says she wrote down verbatim what your mother told her, and the interview was conducted, as we can see -- or the report compiled, rather, on the 9th of April. And one sees at the bottom of the page that the record shows that the interview was conducted also on the 9th of April at a youth centre in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just go to the second page, please, and to the first paragraph. If you can just enlarge the first paragraph, please. Just the first paragraph is all we need for the present purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In the third line of the first paragraph, I'm going to read this slowly for translation purposes. "They caught my son Dragoslav at the end of February. They stopped him, took his pistol, and then gave it back. It was four armed and masked men who stopped him, asked him where he lived and things like that. They searched him and found the pistol. They gave it back but made him sign a paper saying they had given the gun back and didn't give him a hard time. It happened in Gllogjan" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that you are reading slowly, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll let the translators catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "It happened in Gllogjan at half past 11.00 at night. They spoke Albanian, not the Siptar used in these parts. We all speak Siptar, but they talked like they do in Albania. They asked their chief: 'Do we give him his gun back?' The chief stood in the dark wearing a mask. They gave my son his gun and ammunition, a cigarette to light up, and wished him God speed. Then he signed. He had to write everything down in Albanian and sign." That is what your mother is recorded as having told a person who interviewed her on the 9th of April of 1998, Mr. Stojanovic. She -- I think you will --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a statement to the police about this incident. I never spoke to journalists about this. As to what my mother said, well, that is something that you should perhaps ask her. What I said here is identical in every respect to the statement that I had made to the police. So what I'm saying is they never mistreated me. They made me write this one; one of them dictated the statement to me. The crux of the matter being I was not mistreated on that particular occasion. They didn't find a gun on me for the simple reason that I had none on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you discuss what had happened to you with your mother?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't. My mother was often left on her own, and I didn't want to cause her to feel more fear than was strictly necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know where she could have got all the details in this account about masked men offering you a packet of cigarettes, requiring you to sign a piece of paper, requiring you to write in Albanian, and so forth? Do you know where she might have got all that kind of information if she didn't get it from you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose I'll need to ask her, shan't I? I didn't know about this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But can you help us about this? Why would your mother ever think that you had a pistol in your car at any time if, as you tell us, it was her pistol and was always left at home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, the only gun in that house belonged to her. I was on two separate occasions, actually, licensed to go and buy myself a gun, but I never did. Those were peaceful times. I didn't think that I would ever need one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, but my question, Mr. Stojanovic, is this: If it was her gun and you never took it away from the home, can you think of any reason why your mother would be under the impression that you could have had a pistol in your car when you were stopped?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this is probably something that you will need to raise with her. I never discussed this with her, nor indeed did I know about this. First I hear of it, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us your mother was -- also kept a rifle in the house. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, a hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you have ammunition for the pistol at the house? Your mother refers to ammunition in the report. Did you have ammunition for the pistol at the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure we did, but I'm not positive. Truth to tell, I wasn't really interested at all. I had been on great terms with all those who later punished me. I never needed to have any weapon on me or ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me move on, Mr. Stojanovic, to another related topic. In the statement that you made to the Prosecution in May 2002, you said that during January and February 1998, you and your family noticed a lot of trucks coming and going from the Haradinaj family compound. Can I ask you this: Did you ever pass that information on to the police, about the coming and going of these trucks to your neighbour's house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Why would I do anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What about your brother Predrag, the police officer, did you never discuss it with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother Predrag wasn't working in the area. I don't think he could have been involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you never discussed with him the fact that there were -- there was a build-up of trucks going backwards and forwards to your neighbours, the Haradinajs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What on earth for? I didn't know what was inside that truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, we'll come to that in just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we please call up Defence identification 020733.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Stojanovic, this is an aerial photo directly over your house and the Haradinaj compound, so that we can see exactly what the relationship between the two is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D24, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a fairly recent photograph. And if we look to the bottom left of that picture, can you see that building which is in ruins, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one do you mean, the largest one or the one over here?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me just orientate you for a moment. You can see the road running vertically on the left-hand side of the photograph from the top to the bottom. Can you see that road; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you can see the road that branches off to the right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at the end of that road, I'm going to suggest to you that is the Haradinaj family compound, although as you've rightly pointed out earlier on this afternoon, part of it has been built on since you lived there. Now, you've told us about two other buildings that were on the Haradinaj --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "if." I said "if," if this is the house, then it must have been built on. It wasn't as big as this. It did have a top floor, but it wasn't quite as spick-and-span as it looked to me in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're right, you said "if," but the Chamber learned from the parties that, as a matter of fact, the house was extended. So therefore, Mr. Emmerson puts this to you not because you said so but because this information reached the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear, so that you can remind yourself, Mr. Stojanovic, if you see the large building, the -- it -- roughly halfway along it is a line in white at an angle, and everything above that line was built after you last lived there, but everything below that white line, so roughly half of the building, the bottom half as it shows on the photograph, was in the same position at the time that you lived there. You would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the previous photograph, I would be able to tell you precisely what was there and what was not; on the one that we saw today, I could tell you exactly what was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can very happily look at that photograph in a little while. I just want to get your orientation for the purposes of these questions. The other two buildings that are shown just either side of that winding road, you told us that there were two other buildings on the Haradinaj family property; one which had been built 20 or 30 years ago, and one which was newer. At the bottom of the two, I suggest, is the one that had been built 20 or 30 years ago and was nearer to your property; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, just a moment. And the third one, and the third barn, too. So three buildings existed at Haxhi Haradinaj's property and Ermin's was next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm not contradicting you. And the smaller building up towards the top of the photograph above the windy road, that was there at that time as well, was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whose house is it because I can't really discern it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I'm not going to give evidence about that, Mr. Stojanovic. Towards the bottom of the picture, towards the bottom of the picture -- Mr. Stojanovic, towards the bottom of the picture, if you can see to the left-hand side is the -- is a building or the ruins of a building by the road. Do you see that, the bottom left-hand side of the picture?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the ruins, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that, I suggest, is the position at which your family home stood in 1998?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- well, maybe, given its condition because I'm sure that your client protected it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think we don't need to bandy remarks like that, Mr. Stojanovic, when all of the buildings in that area were destroyed in the course of the war. So perhaps we can keep ourselves to the questions that we're asking and answering?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but his was not, and now when I see what he done to my house I have to say things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I do understand what makes you make these kind of observations, but the Chamber would very much like to -- you to answer the questions put to you by Mr. Emmerson. Please try to focus on that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this lower row of bushes, Mr. Stojanovic, that we can see at an angle going down towards the bottom right-hand corner of the photograph, that's the border of your property, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we can get a sense, it's -- of the distance between the two, your property extended right up to the edge of where those bushes appear?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The police during this time were visiting your home twice a week, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police did not come to my house. They passed by the road, so the information you had is correct. They would pass by. We were the only Serb house in the area and they would stop by, talk to us, ask us if anything was amiss, if anyone was mistreating us, and I was the man of the house and it was my duty - it was our custom - for me to invite them into the house to offer them coffee and I would do the same thing to my Albanian neighbours. This is what I did on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did they not ask you at any time to report anything suspicious that you'd seen, being so close to the Haradinaj family home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, if they had asked us to report this and if this had been done on time, none of this would have happened. Nobody asked me to do that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence somebody called Miloica Vlahovic. You know Miloica Vlahovic, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milovan Vlahovic, I don't recall ever having mention -- mentioned someone by the name of Miloica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My fault then. Do you know Miloica Vlahovic, Mr. Stojanovic? He used to be the teacher in the area. He's the son of Milovan Vlahovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Milovan, I didn't know Miloica. The late Milovan, I attended his funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I be absolutely clear that I've got my pronunciation right. Did you know any of the sons of the family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which of the Vlahovic sons did you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So there may be a pronunciation problem on my part. Did you know Miloica Vlahovic, their son?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Miloica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he was a teacher, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He's given evidence to this Tribunal, Mr. Stojanovic, that your mother, Ljubica, was the first person to discover the fact that there was a KLA military training going on, including weapons training in Gllogjan? Did -- you're smiling. I'm giving you an indication, Mr. Stojanovic, of evidence that's been given on oath by Miloica Vlahovic. I want to understand whether or not your mother ever discussed with you, as she had apparently done with him, that she had discovered the fact that there was KLA training going on in Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what Miloica said, and my mother is an elderly woman. At that time, she was 60, 65 years old. She was working the land. She didn't have any education to speak of, and she was the last person on earth to discover things and to know what was going on, what was not going on. So I really don't know what to tell you on this account.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I ask you this: He's also given evidence that from some very considerable distance away, it was possible to hear the sound of shooting from January onwards intermittently from Gllogjan. Now, you were very close, Mr. Stojanovic, did you hear shooting coming from Gllogjan between January and the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, shooting could be heard, but there were some attacks. But let me state right at the beginning, I didn't see anything at night. There would be attacks on the police station at 8.00 or 9.00. We could hear the gun-fire because the police station was uphill in Rznic, and you could hear sound from quite a distance at night. And I really couldn't tell you what I saw, what I heard, because we would mostly then hear in the media the next day there would be reports that there had been an attack on a police station or something like that. But I can confirm that there was gun-fire, we could hear gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And any gun-fire from the area around the Haradinaj compound at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The station was not at the Haradinajs' house or my house. It was 5 -- 4 or 5 kilometres away from our house; that's where the gun-fire was coming from. So I can't say that it was really very close. And that was up until the 18th of March, or rather, until the 18th of March I didn't hear any gun-fire coming from Haradinaj -- the Haradinaj house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The answer was not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, did you have a telephone in the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What sort of phone was it, can I ask?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a cordless phone, or rather, a mobile phone because there were no telephone lines to the -- in the village. So it was a mobile phone or a cordless phone. Most of my neighbours had one of those. A lot of us had such telephones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you now remember when you first acquired a mobile telephone in the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a mobile phone; it was a cordless phone. There is a difference there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then it may be helpful --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was five or six years -- it was five or six years before the 18th or the 24th of March. I don't really remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to ask you any further questions about this. It may seem a very small matter, but can I just understand. You say it wasn't a mobile phone, it was a cordless phone. What exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a phone that gets hooked up on the line in the -- in the town, and then you can carry it around, around your house, the headset. You can carry the headset with you and then -- it's practically like an ordinary telephone, for all intents and purposes. It's -- there were a lot of such phones in Kosovo in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, where was your telephone hooked up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A friend of mine, Bulatovic, it was in his house. I used his number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the -- the range spread from Djakovica to Gllogjan, to Dubrava?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson, I was just asking your attention. Mr. Emmerson, it would certainly assist the Chamber if you make any reference to testimony by other witnesses to give us the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm very happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- day and the page, so that we can follow what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll give Your Honour a list of the relevant passages during the course of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break now for 20 minutes. We'll resume at five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two procedural matters before we continue. First of all, the Defence is informed that the Chamber is inclined to grant the partly confidential request for videolink and has the following on its mind, that -- yes, I don't think, as a matter of fact, that we have to go into private session for this, but the issue is that -- well, perhaps just out of an abundance of caution, perhaps we should do. It will not take very long.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. One of the issues still not finally decided was the nonsitting days, and I do understand that everyone would very much like to know. It has to do with -- to some extent with normal breaks as every Chamber has, also the nonavailability of some of the Judges during all of the days. Now, let me tell you what we have decided for sure. The first two dates, for the 29th and the 30th of March, the Chamber has decided that on the 29th, that's Thursday, if there is a witness which we would not start a witness on Wednesday and half an hour before -- before adjourning, but if there would be a witness who needs another half an hour or an hour -- one hour and a half, one session, so relatively short, we'll do that on Thursday. So, therefore, we are not sitting if we have -- but we are not going to keep a witness here for quite a lot of days, that would be Thursday, Friday -- five days just to have another half an hour or one hour, one hour and a half of examination. So therefore, the 29th is -- depends on the situation. The 30th, then, we'll not be sitting. Then the 6th and the 9th of April are UN holidays. The 10th, 11th, 12th, and 13th of April, we'll not sit. Then the 30th of April is a UN holiday, and we will not sit on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th of May. 25th of May is a Friday, there it also will depend on whether there's any witness waiting or not. The same is true for the 8th of June, so we might not sit, but if there's a good reason to -- to not keep a witness for the whole of the weekend, just for one hour less -- one hour left, then we might sit on the 25th of May, the 8th of June. Then the 23rd -- the week of the 23rd until the 27th of July, that's the last week before the recess, we will not sit. So uncertain at this moment is the 29th of March, that is this Thursday; the 25th of May; and the 8th of June, these are, I would call it, flexible days. If we would sit on these days, the Chamber would not sit in its normal composition. It would be then two Judges rather than three. Is there any -- is this clear to everyone? Then, Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness into -- yes, Mr. -- I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No problem. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, I'm sure you'll -- I'm very grateful for the clarification in that respect. Your Honour asked me before the break for a transcript reference in respect to the passages that have been put to the witness. It was from the evidence of Miloica Vlahovic. It was page 1571, lines 19 to 22. He was asked to give specific examples of people who had been saying that there was a training ground in Gllogjan and replied: "For example, Ljubica Stojanovic from Dubrava, she was the first to find out about the training ground. Dubrava and Gllogjan are two neighbouring villages. They are adjacent."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was the quotation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I just wanted to come back for a moment to this question about your mother's gun and you mentioned the hunting rifle. I wanted to just ask you about one matter. When you made your statement on the 26th of May, 2006, you referred to an article about your case in a Serbian magazine called "Illustrojana Politika, and the article had been published on the 24th of April, a few days after the incident on the 18th of April. And, presumably, you'd read that article?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I referred to an article? I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, there is a reference in your witness statement --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- in which the following passage appears: "I hand over to Mr. Matti Raatikainen a Serbian magazine "Illustrojana Politika" from the 25th of April, 1998 with an article about our case." In other words, you are recorded as having given that article to the investigator. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, let me make this clear. My brother had the papers. He gave the statement the first day, and then on the second or on the third day -- well, it doesn't matter anyway. We didn't give our statements over a single day. So he gave -- handed over the newspaper because I didn't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. It's possible then that the person concerned made an error in that respect, but you -- can I ask you, please, just to look and see if you recognise the article?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have it on the system, but I think it's easier to hand it to the witness in paper. For the e-court, it is Rule 65 ter Exhibit Number 21, in English and in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, and that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D25, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I've marked a passage for you to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have an English translation perhaps we could call up for -- on the screen, and in English should be linked to it. Sorry, do we have the English translation? Do Your Honours have the English translation on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I have 25th of April, 1998 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- headline, "Metohija, When They Were Taken" --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly, exactly. Could Your Honours turn to the second page of that English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I have to change something to get -- to manipulate it. Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And to a paragraph beginning: "They could be good friends ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The second main paragraph and to the last five lines of that paragraph. And does Your Honour see a sentence beginning: "There was a time" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, this article contains two lengthy interviews which are direct quotation of interviews with your mother and your brother Mijat, and the passage I've marked for you on the Serbian original, can you find the following words, please: "There was a time when I kept a rifle strapped over my shoulder and slept like that, keeping watch over my children. There was a place at the window from where I could take aim when they called out to me and threatened me. They would do it to me and I would do it to them." That is a quotation attributed to your mother. Do you have that in the original?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not a problem. Just read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll read it to you again: "There was a time when I kept a rifle strapped over my shoulder and slept like that, keeping watch over my children. There was a place at the window from where I could take aim when they called out to me and threatened me. They would do it to me and I would do it to them." Do you remember your mother using a rifle from a particular position at the house and aiming at people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us that it was just a hunting rifle. Do you want to reconsider --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just an ordinary hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see anybody pointing it at anybody?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I want to move then if I can, please, to some questions about what happened on the 24th of March. You've told us that your mother called you home from work that day. Can you just clarify for us, please, when you arrived at your home, which members of your family were already there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said this, but let me repeat. My mother, my brother's small child, and my sister, and myself, we arrived; and then later during the day Mijat arrived, too. So that was during the day. I don't know the exact time, because he had gone away to sell this paint.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it may be my mistake. I don't remember you mentioning Mijat --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. I may have forgotten to mention him, but at that time, at any rate, he was not there when I arrived. He may have arrived later. And as for this article that you just quoted to me, I was in hospital when this was published, so I don't really know much about that. As far as I can remember, I was in hospital at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you say that Mijat came later on the 24th of March. Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember how long after you arrived it was that Mijat arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the afternoon. I don't know exactly. I can't really give you an idea as to when it was that he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your young nephew, was that your brother Vladimir's son?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see Vladimir at the house that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had arrived from Decani, because later on my mother called him, the baby was crying, so he got the baby and drove it back to Decani where he lived, just in order to get the baby away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So how long was your brother Vladimir at the property on the 24th of March, for roughly how long?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vladimir stayed for under half an hour, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. And so that I'm clear, are you saying that Vladimir was not there when you arrived back at the house?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when I arrived back?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you arrived back at the house from work, are you saying Vladimir was not there at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vladimir came. After I came, he had driven the baby to Decani. It wasn't before me that he came, it was after me. I was at the house when my mother called him and told him to come and get the baby.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can you give us an approximate time for that, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd be hard-put to remember exactly, but I think about midday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we look, please, at Rule 65 ter number 1162.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D26, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Whilst that document is being brought up, Mr. Stojanovic, can I ask you one or two other questions? Don't worry about it for just a moment. You were -- were asked by Mr. Re on Friday about what had taken place that day, and at one point you said that there was fighting going on. And Mr. Re asked you who the fighting was between, and you told us that there was shooting coming from the Haradinaj house. And you were asked again who was it between, and you said being a civilian, you were barred from going outside. Now, I just want to be clear, and for anyone's note that's at transcript 83, line 20. Can I just be clear about this, Mr. Stojanovic --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, just a minute. I didn't say it was between civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That's true. As a civilian, it was impossible to go out. As for the police and the Haradinajs, who exactly was involved, now that is not something that I can say. I'm certain that they were civilians, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, we can consult the system but only in the continued paging, not 83 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's of the day, but I'll find it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not -- I think if I can just clarify it with the witness what his evidence is, it may resolve the problem, and I think you may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that the Judges are working from different systems, but okay, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be, Mr. Stojanovic, that there was a problem in translating the question to you a moment ago. I wasn't suggesting to you that you had ever said that there was fighting between civilians. What I suggested to you was that you had told us that being a civilian, you were prevented from going outside; and that is what you told us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Only to my yard where my livestock was, out there, around the house, right there. No further.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment. Can we be clear, though, you knew, didn't you, that during the day there was fighting going on between people in the Haradinaj compound, on the one hand, and police on the other; that it was police who were engaged in a gun-battle. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You knew that the police were on your property firing rockets and guns towards the Haradinaj family compound, from your property, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there were no rockets because that's the interpretation that I'm receiving. Rockets were fired on my house from the Haradinaj household, and there was shooting on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You just told us a moment ago, you couldn't see what was going on outside. Are you telling us now that you know the police did not fire rockets towards the Haradinaj house? How would you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that side, you see. Try to picture my terrace, my house, which was the place that I was looking out from. There's an open view of both the Haradinajs' houses. Later on, after the police had left, I was unable to see anything, but for as long as they were around the yard and in the area, I did see things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So now you're telling us, are you, you were able to see the police action from your yard in detail throughout? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Not this entire time, and not in detail. There is my terrace, and you can only see so far. And then later, the police drove them back past their houses and on to the village. The village is quite far away, there is a lot of shrubbery in the area, the photograph clearly shows that, and over there you can't see a thing. The only thing you can hear is the sounds of shooting and firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's just concentrate on what you could see, Mr. Stojanovic. You knew --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the witness's remark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please repeat what you just said, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm only telling you what I was able to see from my terrace or what was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, let's just be clear. You knew that there were large numbers of police officers inside your property shooting from your property towards the Haradinaj compound, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were police on my property, but not just on my property. They were along the road, too, and on all the contiguous properties. Deraj Maljoka's [phoen] meadow, for example, when I drove up there I saw it, so the police were not just on my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your property, though, was the nearest property to the Haradinajs' property, wasn't it, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that's where the largest concentration of police officers took up position to attack the compound, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. The largest concentration was not -- rather, there were police officers. But the largest concentration surely -- not surely, I'm telling you about what I saw. They were by the road-side in ditches along the road, and that was where they took cover or whatever they called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: How many of them were on your property that you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't exactly count them, but I'd say between 10 and 15 or thereabouts. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And can I ask you this: Are you continuing to say that you are sure that the officers on your property did not shoot rockets from your property on to the Haradinajs' compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those in front, those that I could see, no, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And were there other soldiers or paramilitaries or police officers on your property that you couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice any on that day. They were all in blue uniforms, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were you able to see all of them from where you were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite all.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so that we're clear, you mentioned two rockets being shot towards your property from the Haradinaj compound, one of which fell short and one of which missed.
