Can we be clear about this, those rockets were shot -- those rockets were shot after the police had begun to fire at the Haradinaj compound from your property, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at home when the police opened fire. Once I got there, the shooting was already in progress. By the time I got there, the police were there --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was upon my arrival that the two shells were fired. One shell hit the plum tree. There was an orchard with plum trees next to our yard. And the other just whizzed past and exploded between the two buildings, in the space between these two buildings, or rather, it never exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So my question, Mr. Stojanovic, and if you could just see if you can just concentrate on the actual question I'm asking you, is by the time those rockets were shot towards your property, the police on your property were already firing at the Haradinaj property, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was firing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at the second page of this statement from your brother Vladimir Stojanovic, and I'll read you the relevant passages. And I just want to see if it jogs your memory at all about who was there first that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could just enlarge it slightly in the English --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then I shall read it to you. He says -- and this is a statement of an interview with your brother that took place on the 9th of April, just two weeks after this event. He says: "It happened on Tuesday, the 24th of March this year. My brother and mother were in Dubrava, and I took my 4-year-old son over there. I got the tractor out to do some ploughing, but the work didn't go too good and I went back to the house. All of a sudden, I heard gun-fire. I told my mother and the others to get inside the house." I pause there. Do you think it's right, in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I had a different text, "... get inside at once" it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise, it's my misreading.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me just put that again: "I told my mother and others to get inside at once." Can I be clear, and perhaps this helps you with your memory, was in fact your brother Vladimir there at the time when the gun-fire first occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. Excuse me, who gave this statement and just where?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your brother gave it. It -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To whom and where?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your -- well, we're reversing roles a little but let me answer your questions anyway. Your brother gave it to somebody called Marijana Andjelkovic, who wrote his words down verbatim on the 9th of April during an interview which took place, as you can see from the records, in Decani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Verbatim is perhaps not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, there is evidence from Marijana Andjelkovic that she took it down verbatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps if my learned friend can point us to the transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I can certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least a statement was taken by -- by this lady, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just go down -- if we just go down a little further to the following paragraph and the beginning of that: "We called Decani on the radio phone we have in the house, but they had already been informed about what was going on. It was exactly 10.30 a.m." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, although truth to tell I can't read English.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "Those in the neighbour's house fired five or six rockets and hand-launchers at the car and blazed away at it with machine-guns. The shooting lasted for about 15 minutes. Then the police arrived and came into our yard from where they opened fire at the Haradinaj house, in which there were UCK soldiers. When the police in our yard started shooting, they fired twice out of hand-launchers at our house; one missed and the other landed in some branches and went off." Do you see that? Do you understand the passage that I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think there is no Serbian text --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I can see the witness seeking to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: To try to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we be clear, Mr. Stojanovic, are you receiving the translation? Do you follow what I'm saying to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I was just looking at the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you read English?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I was just looking at the Decani bit because that's what I wanted to know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The point is your brother is recorded there as saying that it was when the police started shooting that rockets were fired in the direction of your property, and that one missed and the other landed in some branches and went off. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I was ever saying that the rocket had been fired before. What I said is by the time I got there, there was shooting between the two sides, and then the rocket came flying in. There was firing throughout, and that's what I've been saying. And when I arrived -- the rocket was fired after I had arrived, but I wasn't there throughout. I arrived later. I had been at work in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that night you spent, you told us, at your brother Predrag's apartment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean, when we left the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That night. You told us you left on the 24th of March.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes, yes, when we left.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And over the days that followed, did you learn more about what had happened on the 24th of March in the village of Gllogjan itself and in the nearby village of Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, I arrived in my house, on my own, which is what I said. I came to my house -- to my yard on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put some specific things to you and ask you to respond to them. Did you discover over the days that followed, that the police operation in the village of Gllogjan that day had resulted in the death of three teenage civilians or three teenage Albanians? Let me put it that way. Did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you learn that police in the village of Gllogjan had launched mortar attacks on some of the civilian properties in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you see the damage for yourself in Gllogjan at any point, Mr. Stojanovic, because there was damage, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hadn't been to the village myself, so I didn't look, but the next day when I arrived back in my yard, I saw the journalists arrive and film my house and Ramush's house, among others. But my house, Ramush's house, or Haxhija's house were not damaged, those were the ones that I could see; as for the rest of the village, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Well, I'm going to suggest to you that the Haradinaj house was damaged -- I'm going to suggest to you that the Haradinaj house was damaged and was damaged by rocket fire launched from your property.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm positive that it wasn't, and there's footage to show that. I'm not sure if it was the next evening or the second-next evening, there's the RTS news, there was footage shown of Ramush's house and the weapons found inside the house and uniforms. I personally watched this on RTS, their second evening news programme that night. The house was intact. All I could see was a house which was intact. That applied to his house, to my house, and to Haxhija's house. All of those were intact. As for the other houses in the village, now that is not something that I can address.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us yesterday -- I'm sorry, you told us on Friday, I think, that people from the Haradinaj family were showing these journalists around and showing them the houses, and that somebody who you said was a painter by trade but was taking photographs --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. The decorator. When we say decorator, that means he was a photographer. A photographer, okay, that's the word I was looking for. Cacaj from Decani, yes, I sort of knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it was a photographer, and people from the Haradinaj family, you say - although not Ramush - were showing this photographer their buildings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see Ramush, but there were plenty of other people, too. It was quite well organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From what you could see, what was it about the buildings on the Haradinaj compound that they were directing the photographer's attention to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the photographs had been taken, I read the article, and I learned that, as you suggest, those two or three men had been killed. It was in "Zeri Rinis," it was in "Rilindja," in all these newspapers. There were these articles.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, one of the statements that your mother has made refers to some newspaper articles that she read, in which she said that the newspapers were writing that she had been informing the police about movements on the Haradinaj compound. She's quoted as having said that she read that in the newspapers, Mr. Stojanovic. Now, can we be clear about this, did you know that there was a perception in Gllogjan that you and your family were responsible for providing information which resulted in the attack on the village that day? Did you know that was a perception in the village?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, that is not true at all. My mother was never anyone's informer ever. I underline that, not ever. Everybody can continue to think whatever they like. She's just a simple country woman who wanted to preserve her own household and her property. On top of that, she, as a woman, had no idea what the men were about doing, regardless of whether we're talking about Dubrava or any other village. It was some sort of an unwritten law. Men and women were never, or almost never, together at the same time in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Stojanovic, I'd like you to listen to my question because I didn't ask you whether it was true. I read to you a passage from a statement from your mother in which she refers to allegations in the newspaper, and the question that I asked you was whether you knew when you, for example, went back to Gllogjan, that people in that village thought your family was responsible for the attack that had been launched in Gllogjan on the 24th of March, whether you knew when you went to the village that that was a perception that the villagers held about your family?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you told us, I think yesterday, that you were aware of helicopters --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours. I'm very close to finishing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You told us yesterday you had seen some helicopters. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you later hear that those helicopters had been used to spray bullets at civilians in the areas of Irzniq and Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once they had infiltrated that police officer, the helicopters were gone; they took them back to Pristina. A helicopter is not silent enough for one not to hear it flying that nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear allegations at any point that helicopters had been used to shoot at civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers, could -- maybe Mr. Emmerson could clarify exactly when he's talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I said "at any time."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the question a moment ago was: "Did you later hear that those helicopters had been using bullets at civilians?" It's quite important for the progress of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- did you ever hear anything about these helicopters being used for firing at civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I hear it; no, I didn't. Did I see it; no, I didn't either. Perhaps they did, for all I know, but I didn't actually see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question is whether you ever heard such a thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you hear an allegation, Mr. Stojanovic, that teachers and children in the school had been detained and then used as human shields by the police, the children in the school? Did you hear that allegation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there's a -- might be a mistake on the transcript. I think the witness answered my question in the negative; whereas it appears as "yes" on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's definitely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Line 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In relation to the school, Mr. Stojanovic, I'm going to read to you a passage from a record of an interview with your mother by the same person who interviewed her on the 9th of April, in which it's recorded that she said that her son Predrag took part in the action in Gllogjan and that he entered the school. Now, can I ask you this: Did you know whether Predrag took part in the police action in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you saw him that night, though, didn't you? You stayed the night with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, but this is not the sort of thing that Predrag is likely to share with me. He doesn't share any of his police work with me, nor would I ever think to ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you spent the night of the 24th of March with your brother Predrag after these events had taken place at your home. Is it your evidence that you didn't discuss what had happened that day with him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. It wasn't that night. I arrived about 12.00 or 1.00. They had held us back, wanting us to make statements about what had occurred, and it wasn't before we had given those statements that they allowed us to leave, the SUP, I mean. So I spent the night at his wife's and children's. He arrived later, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've got just two further questions on this if that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can finish within two, three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss those events with Predrag on the next day or the days that followed, the events on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, I hadn't seen Predrag in a long time, and then the war broke out. I was in hospital, and then after I had left hospital, he spent quite a long time away from Decani; therefore, we didn't talk. And to be quite frank, I didn't really want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So just to be clear, is it your evidence that between the 24th of March and the 18th of April, when you were injured, you never discussed with Predrag what had occurred on the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. We didn't really see that much of each other anyway, after that evening, after that night. We didn't see each other at all, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And do you know now whether he took part in the police action in Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was a policeman, and this is something that I said before, not just now, I don't mean just now. He was a police officer, as many of our neighbours from Glodjane were. When Siptars were still serving on that same police force, they all worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Could I just get an impression on how much time the other counsel would need? Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No more than Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, no less either. Then there was some merit in what Mr. Re said about verbatim. What the witness said was about his interview, she said and it was about firing rockets: "I don't recall that because I would have certainly noted that. Most of the things, again I have to say I noted verbatim," that's not exactly the same as making it verbatim and apart from what finally was put on paper, whether that was verbatim, yes or no, it was about notes. So this being clarified. You find that on page 648, line 5. We -- before we adjourn, Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your evidence. We'd like to see you back -- Mr. Re, unless there would be no need for re-examination, because I see that there's no further cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I do have a little bit of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. So tomorrow it will, most likely, not take very long tomorrow, but we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom, and you are again instructed not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have already given or you're still about to give. We stand adjourned until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of March, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.,
